title: H. G. Wells: The War of the Worlds — Ep 13/27 — "How I Fell in with the Curate"
description:
The War of the Worlds, Episode 13. Stung by the loss at Shepperton, the Martians fall back to their pit on Horsell Common, and the green smoke climbs while fresh fighting machines stand sentinel. On Richmond Hill the guns are dug in, and a heliograph winks across the valley.

Scalded and half-senseless, the narrator finds a small boat drifting empty down the steaming Thames and paddles it past burning Halliford, through smoke and reeds on fire, until at Walton bridge his fever beats his fear and he crawls ashore into the long grass.

He wakes at sunset beside a stranger: a curate in soot-smudged shirt sleeves, staring at a flicker of light in the sky. "What does it mean? What do these things mean?" His church is gone, his parish burned in one afternoon, and his faith is going with it. "Be a man!" says the narrator. "One of them was killed yonder, not three hours ago."

Chapter XIII of Book One of H. G. Wells's The War of the Worlds (1898), "How I Fell in with the Curate", in the public domain.

— The Keeper's Lantern —
Every episode is one whole chapter, in order, from the first page to the last.
